_comment: The css-backgrounds-3 §3.6 percentage rule: a percentage P does NOT mean 'P of the positioning area'. It aligns the P point of the IMAGE with the P point of the AREA, so the used offset is (area_size - image_size) * P. The naive reading (area_size * P) agrees only at 0%, which is why it survives so easily. `background-position` is absent from fixtures/visual-test.json, and the existing fixtures/properties/background/background-position.json covers keywords plus a single 50% 50% case with no stated expectation and no oversized image, so the sign-flipping half of the rule — a NEGATIVE used offset whenever the image is larger than the area — is untested anywhere. Every box is 200x100 with a light #ecf0f1 backdrop and one no-repeat tile whose gradient runs left-to-right (#e74c3c -> #2c3e50) so its orientation and its clipped edges are both readable. Offsets and colours are component-local (the web canvas adds (16,16)); sample below y=20 to stay clear of the block-font label band. MUST MATCH: BgPosPct_Keyword_Center == BgPosPct_50_50 and BgPosPct_Keyword_RightBottom == BgPosPct_100_100 (§3.6 defines `center` as 50% and `right`/`bottom` as 100%), so a keyword path that does not route through the percentage arithmetic shows up as an inequality inside one platform.

BgPosPct_50_50._note: SPEC offset ((200-40)*0.5, (100-20)*0.5) = (80,40): the 40x20 tile occupies x 80..120, y 40..60, centred. NAIVE (area*P) offset (100,50) puts it at x 100..140, y 50..70 — a 20px/10px shift, fully separable. Sample (100,50) = tile gradient midpoint, (60,50) = #ecf0f1.

BgPosPct_100_100._note: SPEC offset ((200-40)*1, (100-20)*1) = (160,80): the tile sits flush in the bottom-right corner, x 160..200, y 80..100. NAIVE offset (200,100) places it entirely outside the box, so the tile is INVISIBLE and the component is a flat #ecf0f1 rectangle. The strongest single row in the file: present-and-flush versus absent.

BgPosPct_25_75._note: Asymmetric percentages so a coincidental pass on 50/50 cannot repeat. SPEC offset (160*0.25, 80*0.75) = (40,60): tile at x 40..80, y 60..80. NAIVE offset (50,75): x 50..90, y 75..95.

BgPosPct_Keyword_Center._note: §3.6: `center` is defined as 50%. EXPECTED byte-identical to BgPosPct_50_50 apart from the block-font label, whose glyphs differ because the component names differ; compare below y=20. An inequality means the keyword and percentage arms compute position differently.

BgPosPct_Keyword_RightBottom._note: §3.6: `right` and `bottom` are defined as 100%. EXPECTED equal to BgPosPct_100_100 below y=20 — tile flush in the bottom-right corner. Note the trap this row sets: if a platform gets the keyword right by special-casing it to 'flush to the corner' while getting the percentage wrong, BgPosPct_100_100 goes blank and this row does not, which points straight at the arithmetic.

BgPosPct_Oversized_50._note: The negative-offset half of the rule. A 300x150 image in a 200x100 area at 50% gives offset ((200-300)*0.5, (100-150)*0.5) = (-50,-25), so the image is CENTRED and overflows on all four sides: the box is fully covered, no #ecf0f1 anywhere. Visible window is image x 50..250, so the left column is at image t = 1/6 = (200,74,63) and the right column at t = 5/6 = (75,64,77). Sample y=50. NAIVE offset (100,50) instead leaves the left 100px and top 50px as bare #ecf0f1 and starts the ramp at pure #e74c3c (231,76,60) — an unmissable difference, and it also catches any implementation that clamps a computed offset to >= 0.

BgPosPct_Oversized_100._note: Same oversized image at 100%: offset ((200-300)*1, (100-150)*1) = (-100,-50), aligning the image's bottom-right corner with the box's. Visible window is image x 100..300, so the left column is t = 1/3 = (169,71,67) and the right column is the end stop #2c3e50 = (44,62,80) exactly. Sample y=50. NAIVE offset (200,100) puts the image wholly outside and leaves a flat #ecf0f1 box.
